evidence.core/CORE-REVIEW.txt:
BOUNCER CORE IMPLEMENTATION AND REVIEW
Candidate: vipirc 0.7.29 / onekeyirc 0.1.28

Owned files, identical in both packages:
  src/app.c, src/app.h, src/protocol.c, src/protocol.h
  tests/test_app.c, tests/test_bouncer_core.c
Final file hashes: owned-file-hashes.json.
Final app.c SHA256:
  d4ab995f789e91d0f08546dddf97cfed85700704f4c046a25be33bf852cd2fe8

IMPLEMENTED BEHAVIOR

Explicit ZNC mode composes account[@client]/network:password only in memory
after the existing verified-TLS credential loader completes. The combined
PASS value must fit the existing 503-byte password bound. Temporary identity,
combined password and outgoing queue storage are wiped. Explicit soju mode
derives SASL PLAIN authcid as account/network[@client], using the existing
SASL password loader and existing registration gate. The config module owns
validation and formatting; the App fixture only provides a concise formatter
double, with separate real-config integration handled by the parent.

Connection-scoped pending settings include bouncer type, user, network,
client id and automatic-away opt-in. Changing account, network or bouncer
type invalidates an unchanged old autocommand list, like changing endpoint.
Automatic reconnect retains the established connection snapshot.

Capabilities have distinct offered, pending and active states. Multiline
LS is accumulated, optional ACKs may arrive separately from required SASL,
and successful SASL does not finish CAP before outstanding replies resolve.
Requested capabilities are SASL when configured, multi-prefix, server-time,
batch and znc.in/self-message when offered. No echo-message, chathistory or
znc.in/playback capability is requested. CAP DEL removes active optional
state; CAP NEW is left for the next connection. Required authentication
does not silently fall back.

IRCv3 tags use case-sensitive exact keys, final-occurrence semantics and
standard unescaping. Server-time is validated as a UTC calendar timestamp
before display, including month/day/leap-year bounds and leap seconds. It
is rendered to seconds with an explicit UTC suffix, without time_t conversion.
Unknown or invalid timestamps use the existing receipt-time display.

Sixteen fixed batch slots with 64-byte case-sensitive references support
nested and interleaved groups. chathistory and znc.in/playback mark historical
content; children inherit that designation. Chat/actions stream through the
existing bounded history instead of accumulating a second message buffer.
Historical input cannot change membership, nick, authentication, away state,
or cause PONG/DCC handling. History suppresses mentions/unread activity.
Unknown batch types process ordinary events individually; an unknown batch
reference is conservatively display-only. Malformed/inconsistent framing or
active-slot exhaustion disconnects with a diagnostic. Disconnect resets state.

Explicit bouncer mode accepts restored own JOINs without the direct-server
late/unrequested JOIN rejection, and skips configured autojoin on downstream
registration. Manual JOIN and configured autocommands remain deliberate.
Own-prefix remote private messages use the target query, with the existing
bounded unsolicited-query allowance. Remote copies no longer replace the
last-locally-sent catch-up anchor.

/znc [COMMAND] sends one paced PRIVMSG to *status; /soju [COMMAND] sends one
to BouncerServ. Empty arguments send help. Matching live mode, registration,
verified TLS and soju authentication are required. /msg *module in ZNC mode
and /msg BouncerServ in soju mode use the same bounded private-control path.
Commands are never split into multiple executable messages. They have no
local own-echo, persistent copy or catch-up anchor; /cancel uses the ordinary
queue. General IRC nick/target validation was not weakened.

Direct app_plan/app_send_plan calls from literal/full composers obey those
same service rules. This closed a concrete bypass of app_command's initial
control handling. BouncerServ plans are conservatively excluded by the pure
history-privacy predicate even if inspected after a connection changes.
Service replies remain visible in the server view but are not persisted.

Independent review reproduced an own-prefix service echo/replay retaining and
persisting command text in both modes. Early own-service suppression fixes
that path. The independent before/after fixture measured retained and persisted
live/history canaries: all four values changed from one to zero in both modes.
This is a controlled server-frame reproduction, not evidence that ordinary
ZNC or soju actually echoes these particular commands.

Per-profile bouncer automatic-away defaults off. Generation and timer wakeups
respect that choice, while manual away and clearing an already-applied
automatic away retain existing semantics.

VALIDATION

results.json contains 16 final compile/run groups: all PASS, with identical
source hashes before/after each execution. Matrix: new bouncer core, existing
App, presence cancellation, presence recovery; both source packages; normal
and ASan/UBSan. Eight sanitizer outputs have both sanitizer symbol families
verified via nm. Runtime options: detect_leaks=0 and halt_on_error=1.

The new core test contains eight groups covering tag/time boundaries,
exact ZNC/SASL wire identity, fragmented CAP acceptance/rejection, password
length/GPG registration ordering, playback and live-state isolation, batch
count/malformed/nesting limits, hidden service commands and echoes, direct
plan entry points, automatic-away gating and configuration staging.

Development records are preserved:
  attempt-1-before-direct-plan-review
  attempt-2-before-own-service-review
The first matrix accidentally built the historical test_app fixture with
ONEKEY_ONLY for the standalone source. Its full-manual assertions failed;
the package's established test_app target deliberately omits that define.
The final runner follows that target. The other standalone focused tests
continue to use ONEKEY_ONLY. These two fixture-mode failures were not client
crashes and are not counted as final passing executions.

LIMITS

This core matrix uses deterministic transport and credential doubles. Parent
tests cover the actual TLS/PTY frontends separately. Native platform,
real-bouncer and real-GnuPG results must not be inferred from this matrix.
Legacy playback with timestamps but no recognized batch framing cannot be
reliably distinguished from delayed live messages; it retains ordinary live
semantics. Dynamic network discovery, explicit history-fetch extensions and
legacy vendor-specific server-time variants were not added.

Protocol contracts consulted:
https://ircv3.net/specs/extensions/batch
https://ircv3.net/specs/extensions/server-time
https://ircv3.net/specs/extensions/message-tags
evidence.core/DOCS-CROSS-REVIEW.txt:
FINAL DOCUMENTATION / FAILURE-PATH CROSS-REVIEW
Review date: 2026-11-16 UTC

Scope

Read-only follow-up against frozen shared core in vipirc 0.7.29 and
onekeyirc 0.1.28. Reviewed doc/BOUNCERS.txt, the release additions to README.md,
CHANGELOG.md and each man page, and the new Makefile.in bouncer targets.
Also traced CAP timeout, server authentication rejection, staged settings,
disconnect state clearing and automatic versus explicit reconnect.
No production source or documentation was edited during this follow-up.

Result

No material mismatch between the reviewed claims and the implemented core
was found. No new blocking regression was identified by this bounded review.
The implementation remains frozen at the hashes in owned-file-hashes.json.

Claims checked

- ZNC composes the supplied account/client/network identity and password
  into the bounded PASS payload; soju derives the SASL identity and requires
  authentication before accepting registration. Both explicit modes use
  the existing verified TLS and password-source paths.
- Bouncer-restored memberships are accepted and the ordinary saved-channel
  autojoin is skipped. Explicit local joins and startup commands remain.
- Automatic-away generation is opt-in per bouncer profile; manual presence
  commands and clearing an already-applied automatic away remain available.
- /znc and /soju require the matching connected mode. Service commands take
  one bounded paced frame, have no local echo, and do not set a catch-up
  anchor. Service replies appear in the server view without persistent-log
  output. Own-prefix service echoes are suppressed, including replay.
- server-time, batch, multi-prefix and offered znc.in/self-message are
  negotiated. echo-message, draft/chathistory and znc.in/playback are not
  requested as capabilities. Playback batch recognition is separate.
- Active batches are bounded at 16 with references at most 64 bytes. The
  core holds no extra unbounded message backlog. Known history suppresses
  protocol actions and current-state changes. Unknown references are
  conservatively display-only; unknown batch types retain ordinary behavior.
- Valid server timestamps render explicitly in UTC. Invalid values fall
  back to local receipt time and never drive internal clocks or pacing.
- Existing direct configurations retain their non-bouncer behavior.
- Documentation explicitly distinguishes protocol fixtures from tests
  against installed ZNC/soju packages or a real IRCNow account.

Build-target check

check-bouncers builds and runs the config, core, commands and guided-setup
fixtures. Its core prerequisite includes tests/test_app.c, which the focused
fixture includes. Source lists reuse the existing fixture link dependencies.

check-bouncers-sanitize instruments both compilation and linking with
address/undefined sanitizers and runs those fixtures plus the stream test.
The one-key command/setup/stream targets retain -DONEKEY_ONLY. Core builds
use the same shared-core fixture mode as the existing test_app target.

check-bouncers-terminal invokes the appropriate real executable and supplies
--full for vipirc. check-efficiency includes the stream fixture in addition
to its existing roster/history prerequisites. The new full-settings targets
link the platform's real curses library. Install/uninstall and clean entries
cover the new bouncer documentation, examples and test outputs.

Failure-path observations

- Optional CAP negotiation has a 15-second deadline. With no required SASL,
  timeout ends negotiation and discards pending optional capability bits.
- Required SASL timeout disconnects with no automatic retry. This includes
  the conservative case where authentication succeeded but an optional
  requested capability never received ACK/NAK before the deadline.
- Required SASL NAK, unsupported mechanisms, withdrawal before success,
  failure numerics, and premature registration do not fall back to an
  unauthenticated session.
- Numeric 464/465 disconnects and stops automatic retry when --reconnect
  is enabled. Without that option it is displayed but the transport is not
  closed immediately by this handler; absent further registration it waits
  for server close/ERROR or the 60-second registration timeout. This is
  inherited unchanged from both baselines, not a new bouncer behavior.
- The registration timeout does not automatically retry a connection that
  uses server credentials or required SASL. Pre-registration ERROR also
  stops retry. Transient transport failure still uses the established
  bounded retry policy.
- All five bouncer settings participate in effective configuration and
  staging. Automatic reconnect uses the running connection snapshot;
  the next explicit connect validates and adopts staged settings. Invalid
  candidates leave staged settings intact. A destination/account/network
  change clears an unchanged inherited startup-command list.
- Disconnect/new-connection initialization clears active capabilities,
  pending capability bits, batch references, authentication and queued
  output, preventing connection-local state from leaking into reconnect.

This follow-up is a source/document cross-check, not an additional execution
claim. The final executed core matrix remains 16 passed, 0 failed, recorded
in results.json, with normal and ASan/UBSan runs for both clients. The known
platform and real-bouncer limits in CORE-REVIEW.txt continue to apply.

evidence.stability/REVIEW.txt:
VIPIRC / ONEKEYIRC: INDEPENDENT STABILITY AND BOUNCER REVIEW
Date: 2026-11-16

Scope

Working trees: bouncer-work/vipirc-0.7.29 and onekeyirc-0.1.28.
Baselines: bouncer-baseline/vipirc-0.7.28 and onekeyirc-0.1.27.
Reviewed the previous SECURITY-DEEP-REVIEW-2026-11-16.txt before starting;
previous TLS/credential/presence fixes are not claimed as new findings.

No public IRC connection, real bouncer account, live credential helper or
installed ZNC/soju daemon was used by this review. Local probes used actual
selected production functions with explicitly described doubles or real
private temporary files. Parent owns real loopback TLS/PTY integration.

Completed fixes, mirrored in both projects

1. Application-wide composer preference propagation.

   src/client.c had omitted composer_fullscreen from load_profile,
   client_new_config and client_add although client_interface_apply treats
   it as an application preference. The immutable baseline probe reported
   composer_fullscreen=0, expected=1 for each new/add/reload path.

   Three narrow assignments now propagate the primary interface preference.
   Source locations at freeze: client.c lines 90, 263 and 291.

   tests/test_client.c checks new/existing/lazy/add/save/reload/startup,
   failed-save preservation, and switching the preference off again. Its new
   bouncer_profile_isolation test also verifies that account/network/client,
   bouncer mode, automatic-away opt-in and credentials remain per-profile;
   a newly created profile receives none of the primary bouncer credentials.
   These tests use actual client/config/profile logic with App doubles.

2. Avoid retained-stream rescans on quiet event-loop wakeups.

   stream_output previously walked all retained records on every WATCH wake
   even when nothing new could be displayed. Retained ring sequences remain
   consecutive when text is cleared, so the first unshown sequence directly
   identifies the starting index. No new cache/allocation/state was added.
   Notices and gap handling retain priority. A ring spanning uint64_t wrap
   retains the original bounded walk. Existing wrap semantics are preserved;
   this does not certify arbitrary 2^64-record session behavior.

   Source location at freeze: idle.c stream_output, lines 693 and 719 onward.
   The new fixture compares bytes, cursor movement and notice state against
   the immutable-baseline linear traversal. It covers empty/quiet rings,
   gaps/eviction, physical ring wrap, cleared text holes, selected-channel
   and mentions filters, 64-record emission batches, output pressure,
   display-mode changes, formatting/encoding and sequence-wrap fallback.

   A component benchmark performs 100000 quiet calls with 2048 retained
   records. The final optimized runs measured 188.832 ms versus 0.344 ms
   (vipirc) and 230.485 ms versus 0.475 ms (onekeyirc), linear versus indexed.
   These are fixture timings for one function, not whole-client speedups,
   power savings, network throughput or a latency guarantee.

3. Compact rendering of bouncer server-time records.

   Independent core review found that protocol.c emits explicit UTC time,
   while both idle formatters expected only the older local timestamp form.
   Compact mode therefore kept the full source/date/channel prefix for
   server-time messages. The direct production-format probe reproduced this.

   One shared compact_record helper now recognizes both existing local and
   explicit UTC timestamps. It preserves UTC and the [history] marker while
   dropping redundant origin/date/target text. Full mode keeps original
   records. Unknown or malformed formats remain intact.

   Source locations: idle.c compact_record line 626, stream_text line 663,
   catchup_display_text line 1279. Tests cover messages/actions/notices,
   queries/mentions, full-mode preservation, actual scrollback measurement
   and frame drawing, and a real temporary log through the catch-up scanner
   and frame renderer. No terminal emulation or ncurses is claimed here.

Independent bouncer core security finding

Own-nick server echoes/history sent to a bouncer control service bypassed
the outgoing hidden-control policy: a synthetic own-prefix PRIVMSG to *sasl
or BouncerServ was retained and written to optional disk logs. Incoming
service-source replies were already excluded; own-source service-target
echoes were the missing boundary.

Before probe: stable app.c 2d7e211a177f8e3d51cba92c553cbe92f1aa667b476e9437a6a284d8c70c3843.
Both ZNC and soju reported retained_live=1, retained_history=1,
persisted_live=1 and persisted_history=1 for temporary fake canaries.

The core owner added an early own-nick plus bouncer-target suppression before
ordinary rendering and CTCP handling, with live/history tests in both modes.
After probe: stable app.c d4ab995f789e91d0f08546dddf97cfed85700704f4c046a25be33bf852cd2fe8.
The identical probe now reports all four values as zero in both modes.
This demonstrates robust handling of synthetic server frames. It does not
claim that ordinary ZNC/soju instances emit such frames.

Read-only review also covered bounded batch state/parent handling, optional
and required CAP acknowledgement state, UTC parser bounds/calendar checks,
historical membership/away/authentication/DCC suppression, service command
authentication gates, staged profile settings, and direct send-plan privacy.
No additional concrete blocker was found in those inspected paths. This is
a focused code review and regression campaign, not a security certification.

Validation evidence

- environment.json: compiler/dependency/socket capability observations.
- probe_composer_inheritance.c and probe_composer_baseline: baseline failure.
- client-checks.json: both clients normal and ASan/UBSan, all four PASS;
  source fingerprints stable before/after each run.
- stream-checks.json: original traversal comparison on immutable vipirc
  baseline and both candidates normal/sanitized, all five PASS.
- stream-compact-checks.json: final source, both clients normal and
  ASan/UBSan, all four PASS with stable fingerprints.
- compact-format-before-after.json: before/after actual UTC/history output.
- control-replay-before.json and control-replay-after.json: independent
  incoming own-service retention/persistence reproduction and correction.
- run_client_checks.py and run_stream_checks.py: reproducible local runners.
- owned-hashes.json: final mirrored owned-file hashes.
- vip-make-results.json and vip-make-*.json/.log: final selected shared
  Makefile targets in the vipirc tree, with strict Linux flags and no curses
  libraries. All five command groups PASS with stable C/header fingerprints.
  These compile and run bouncer config/core/commands/setup, roster,
  disk catch-up, retained stream and existing client regression fixtures
  normally and with ASan/UBSan. Sanitizer symbols were verified in the
  generated binaries. This includes complete shared-source link recipes,
  beyond the earlier isolated stream function checks.

ASan leak detection was disabled; address/undefined-behavior checks were
enabled with halt-on-error. Strict compiler warnings were treated as errors.
The stream fixture uses function/data sections and linker garbage collection
in the earlier focused runner to isolate actual production stream/catch-up
code. The later Makefile runs link the established shared-source fixture
recipes normally. Neither fixture is a full client executable.

The first vipirc Makefile run exposed a test link-recipe omission: the new
stream target reused the catch-up source list without its ONEKEY_ONLY
define, leaving vipirc_manual unresolved. The same define was already
present in both onekeyirc stream recipes. With root authorization, added
ONEKEY_ONLY to the vipirc normal and sanitizer stream recipes only, matching
the established catch-up target. The initial failed build is retained under
attempt-1-vip-stream-link; the complete subsequent matrix passed. The
generated validation Makefile and its exact template/hash/flag substitutions
are preserved. This is not a native vipirc configure or ncurses build pass.

Environment and integration limits

Native AF_UNIX socket creation returns EPERM in this environment. AF_INET
and socketpair creation work. Wide ncurses headers/pkg-config metadata are
absent. This review did not change packages, fake headers, bypass session
socket restrictions or claim a native full-curses validation.

Read-only review of root's test_bouncer_terminal.py found that service
replies correctly route to server view, so waiting in #test for their text
was a fixture error. Recommended checking the exact outbound control wire
line, selecting /server, then observing the reply. Also recommended a final
backlog-record assertion, bounded SASL fixture accumulation, and naming the
own-private replay result precisely. Root owns these fixture changes/runs.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import concurrent.futures
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import time

ROOT = Path("/workspace/scratch/906cef4a9bba")
EVIDENCE = ROOT / "bouncer-validation/core"
SOURCES = ["src/app.c", "src/app.h", "src/protocol.c", "src/protocol.h", "src/config.h"]
TESTS = ["test_bouncer_core", "test_app", "test_presence_cancellation", "test_presence_recovery"]

def one(item):
    project, test, sanitizer = item
    tree = ROOT / "bouncer-work" / project
    label = project + "-" + test + ("-sanitize" if sanitizer else "-normal")
    binary = EVIDENCE / label
    flags = ["-std=c11", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Werror", "-pedantic"]
    # The historical test_app manual assertions intentionally exercise the
    # full-core API. Its established build target omits ONEKEY_ONLY in both
    # packages. Other focused suites also exercise the standalone define.
    if project.startswith("onekey") and test != "test_app":
        flags += ["-DONEKEY_ONLY"]
    flags += ["-O1", "-g", "-fsanitize=address,undefined", "-fno-omit-frame-pointer"] if sanitizer else ["-O2"]
    command = ["cc", *flags, "-Isrc", "-o", str(binary), "tests/" + test + ".c",
               "src/app.c", "src/autocommands.c", "src/sim.c", "src/protocol.c"]
    record = {"label": label, "compile_command": command,
              "source_hashes": {name: hashlib.sha256((tree/name).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for name in SOURCES}}
    started = time.monotonic()
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=tree, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=120)
    record["compile_exit"] = result.returncode
    record["compile_output"] = result.stdout
    if result.returncode == 0:
        env = os.environ.copy()
        env["ASAN_OPTIONS"] = "detect_leaks=0:halt_on_error=1"
        env["UBSAN_OPTIONS"] = "halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1"
        record["runtime_env"] = {key: env[key] for key in ("ASAN_OPTIONS", "UBSAN_OPTIONS")}
        record["run_command"] = [str(binary)]
        result = subprocess.run([str(binary)], cwd=tree, env=env, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=90)
        record["run_exit"] = result.returncode
        record["run_output"] = result.stdout
        if sanitizer:
            symbols = subprocess.run(["nm", "-u", str(binary)], text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, check=True).stdout
            record["asan_symbol_present"] = "__asan_" in symbols
            record["ubsan_symbol_present"] = "__ubsan_" in symbols
    record["elapsed_seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 3)
    record["end_source_hashes"] = {name: hashlib.sha256((tree/name).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for name in SOURCES}
    record["status"] = "PASS" if (record.get("compile_exit") == 0 and record.get("run_exit") == 0 and
        record["source_hashes"] == record["end_source_hashes"] and
        (not sanitizer or (record.get("asan_symbol_present") and record.get("ubsan_symbol_present")))) else "FAIL"
    (EVIDENCE/(label+".json")).write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2)+"\n")
    print(label + " " + record["status"], flush=True)
    return record

items = [(project, test, sanitizer) for project in ("vipirc-0.7.29", "onekeyirc-0.1.28")
         for test in TESTS for sanitizer in (False, True)]
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool:
    records = list(pool.map(one, items))
(EVIDENCE/"results.json").write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=2)+"\n")
raise SystemExit(0 if all(x["status"] == "PASS" for x in records) else 1)

binaries = {

}
root = roots[args.kind]
out = base / "bouncer-validation/setup"
scripts = {"direct": "test_idle_setup.py", "async": "test_setup_async.py", "paths": "test_setup_paths.py"}
command = ["python3", "-u", "tests/" + scripts[args.suite]]
command += (["--full"] if args.kind == "idle" else []) if args.suite == "direct" else ["--mode", args.kind]
environment = os.environ.copy()
environment.update({key: str(value) for key, value in binaries.items()})
environment["PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE"] = "1"
stem = "pty-" + args.kind + "-" + args.suite
log = out / (stem + ".log")
manifest = out / (stem + ".json")
paths = [*binaries.values(), *sorted((root / "src").glob("*.c")), *sorted((root / "src").glob("*.h"))]
paths += [root / "tests" / name for name in [
    "test_idle_setup.py", "test_setup_async.py", "test_setup_paths.py",
    "test_idle_terminal.py", "test_integration.py"]]
hashes = {str(path): hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for path in paths}
record = {
    "command": command, "cwd": str(root),
    "environment_overrides": {key: environment[key] for key in [*binaries, "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE"]},
    "timeout_seconds": 240, "source_and_executable_sha256": hashes,
    "scope": "Real PTYs, local loopback IRC and isolated fake GPG helpers. vipirc uses real idle code with aborting full-UI stubs. No native curses or session AF_UNIX validation.",
    "log": str(log), "state": "running",
}
manifest.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")
print(stem + " started", flush=True)
started = time.monotonic()
with log.open("wb") as stream:
    process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=root, env=environment, stdout=stream, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    try:
        record["exit"] = process.wait(timeout=record["timeout_seconds"])
        record["state"] = "complete"
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        record["state"] = "timeout"
        process.send_signal(signal.SIGINT)
        try:
            record["exit"] = process.wait(timeout=8)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            process.kill()
            record["exit"] = process.wait(timeout=3)
record["seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 3)
record["source_and_executable_unchanged"] = hashes == {
    str(path): hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for path in paths}
manifest.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")
print(stem, record["state"], record["exit"], record["seconds"], "seconds", flush=True)

records=[]
for name in ["test_bouncer_setup","test_idle_setup"]:
    stem=args.kind+"-"+args.mode+"-"+name
    paths=["tests/"+name+".c"]+sources+["src/config.h","src/app.h"]

    binary=out/stem
    for phase,cmd in [("compile",["cc"]+flags+["-o",str(binary)]+["tests/"+name+".c"]+sources+["-lssl","-lcrypto"]),("run",[str(binary)])]:
        start=time.monotonic(); r=subprocess.run(cmd,cwd=root,env=env,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,timeout=180)
        log=out/(stem+"-"+phase+".log"); log.write_bytes(r.stdout)
        after={str(x):hashlib.sha256((root/x).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for x in paths}
        records.append({"case":stem,"phase":phase,"command":cmd,"cwd":str(root),"exit":r.returncode,"seconds":round(time.monotonic()-start,3),"log":str(log),"source_sha256":hashes,"source_unchanged":hashes==after})
        print(stem,phase,r.returncode,flush=True)
        (out/(args.kind+"-"+args.mode+"-results.json")).write_text(json.dumps(records,indent=2)+"\n")
        if r.returncode: raise SystemExit(r.returncode)

"""Validate selected shared targets without claiming native curses configure.

The generated Makefile is kept in the evidence directory. Only the requested
non-curses target recipes are run; production Makefile.in is not modified.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import time

ROOT = Path('/workspace/scratch/906cef4a9bba')
TREE = ROOT / 'bouncer-work/vipirc-0.7.29'
OUT = ROOT / 'bouncer-validation/stability'
MAKEFILE = OUT / 'Makefile.vip-shared-validation'
FLAGS = '-O2 -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -fstack-protector-strong -Wformat=2 -Werror=format-security -fPIE'
SAN = '-O1 -g -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -fstack-protector-strong -Wformat=2 -Werror=format-security -fPIE -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer'
substitutions = {
    'PREFIX': '/usr/local', 'CC': 'cc',
    'CPPFLAGS': '-D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L -D_XOPEN_SOURCE=700 -D_XOPEN_SOURCE_EXTENDED=1 -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2',
    'CFLAGS': FLAGS, 'LDFLAGS': '-pie -Wl,-z,relro -Wl,-z,now -Wl,-z,noexecstack',
    'CURSES_LIBS': '', 'TLS_LIBS': '-lssl -lcrypto'
}
template = (TREE / 'Makefile.in').read_text()
generated = re.sub(r'@([A-Z_]+)@', lambda m: substitutions[m[1]], template)
assert not re.search(r'@[A-Z_]+@', generated)
MAKEFILE.write_text(generated)
sha = lambda path: hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
metadata = {
    'scope': 'Selected non-curses shared Makefile targets. No native vipirc configure, ncurses build, or full UI execution claim.',
    'substitutions': substitutions,
    'source_template_sha256': sha(TREE / 'Makefile.in'),
    'generated_makefile_sha256': sha(MAKEFILE),
    'sanitizer_flags': SAN,
}
(OUT / 'vip-make-metadata.json').write_text(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2) + '\n')

tests = ['test_bouncer_config', 'test_bouncer_core', 'test_bouncer_commands', 'test_bouncer_setup',
         'test_app', 'test_idle_commands', 'test_idle_setup', 'test_idle_stream', 'test_idle_catchup',
         'test_roster', 'test_client']
inputs = sorted(set([*TREE.glob('src/*.c'), *TREE.glob('src/*.h'),
                     *(TREE / 'tests' / (name + '.c') for name in tests)]))
fingerprints = lambda: {str(p.relative_to(TREE)): sha(p) for p in inputs}
env = dict(os.environ, ASAN_OPTIONS='detect_leaks=0:halt_on_error=1',
           UBSAN_OPTIONS='halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1')
base = ['make', '-B', '-f', str(MAKEFILE)]
normal_bins = ['build/test_bouncer_config', 'build/test_bouncer_core', 'build/test_bouncer_commands',
               'build/test_bouncer_setup', 'build/test_roster', 'build/test_idle_catchup',
               'build/test_idle_stream', 'build/test_client']
jobs = [
    ('normal-targets', [*base, '-j2', 'check-bouncers', 'check-efficiency', 'build/test_client'], normal_bins, False),
    ('normal-client', ['./build/test_client'], ['build/test_client'], False),
    ('sanitize-bouncer-targets', [*base, 'SANFLAGS=' + SAN, 'check-bouncers-sanitize'],
     ['build/bouncer-sanitize/' + name for name in ['config', 'core', 'commands', 'setup', 'stream']], True),
    ('sanitize-efficiency-targets', [*base, '-j2', 'CFLAGS=' + SAN, 'check-efficiency', 'build/test_client'],
     ['build/test_roster', 'build/test_idle_catchup', 'build/test_idle_stream', 'build/test_client'], True),
    ('sanitize-client', ['./build/test_client'], ['build/test_client'], True)
]
records = []
for label, command, binaries, sanitizer in jobs:
    print('START vip-shared-' + label, flush=True)
    before = fingerprints()
    began = time.monotonic()
    run = subprocess.run(command, cwd=TREE, env=env, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                         stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=720)
    output_path = OUT / ('vip-make-' + label + '.log')
    output_path.write_text(run.stdout)
    record = {'label': label, 'command': command, 'cwd': str(TREE),
              'source_before': before, 'source_after': fingerprints(),
              'exit': run.returncode, 'seconds': round(time.monotonic() - began, 3),
              'output': run.stdout, 'output_file': str(output_path),
              'generated_makefile_sha256': sha(MAKEFILE),
              'runtime_env': {key: env[key] for key in ['ASAN_OPTIONS', 'UBSAN_OPTIONS']},
              'binaries': {}}
    for name in binaries:
        binary = TREE / name
        if not binary.exists(): continue
        details = {'sha256': sha(binary)}
        if sanitizer:
            symbols = subprocess.run(['nm', '-u', str(binary)], text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                                     stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=30)
            details.update(asan_symbol_present='__asan_' in symbols.stdout,
                           ubsan_symbol_present='__ubsan_' in symbols.stdout)
        record['binaries'][name] = details
    record['source_stable'] = record['source_before'] == record['source_after']
    record['status'] = 'PASS' if run.returncode == 0 and record['source_stable'] and len(record['binaries']) == len(binaries) and (
        not sanitizer or all(b['asan_symbol_present'] and b['ubsan_symbol_present'] for b in record['binaries'].values())) else 'FAIL'
    records.append(record)
    (OUT / ('vip-make-' + label + '.json')).write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + '\n')
    (OUT / 'vip-make-results.json').write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=2) + '\n')
    print(json.dumps({key: record[key] for key in ['label', 'status', 'exit', 'seconds', 'source_stable']}), flush=True)
    if record['status'] != 'PASS':
        print(run.stdout[-6000:], flush=True)
        break

raise SystemExit(0 if len(records) == len(jobs) and all(r['status'] == 'PASS' for r in records) else 1)
